questions.q: A maize farmer near Barentu applies bags of nitrogen fertilizer to a fixed plot of land. The response of the crop is: with $$3$$ bags the total product is $$22\text{ quintals}$$, with $$4$$ bags it is $$28\text{ quintals}$$, with $$5$$ bags it is $$32\text{ quintals}$$ and with $$6$$ bags it is $$34\text{ quintals}$$. Maize sells at $$900\text{ Nakfa}$$ per quintal and each bag of fertilizer costs $$2\,000\text{ Nakfa}$$. (a) Compute the marginal product of the fourth, fifth and sixth bags. (b) Compute the Marginal Value Product for each of those bags. (c) State the profit-maximizing number of bags and explain why applying one more bag would reduce profit.
questions.answer: (a) MP: 4th bag $$= 6$$, 5th bag $$= 4$$, 6th bag $$= 2\text{ quintals}$$. (b) MVP: 4th $$= 5\,400\text{ Nakfa}$$, 5th $$= 3\,600\text{ Nakfa}$$, 6th $$= 1\,800\text{ Nakfa}$$. (c) The profit-maximizing level is $$5$$ bags, because the 5th bag's MVP ($$3\,600\text{ Nakfa}$$) still exceeds the input price ($$2\,000\text{ Nakfa}$$) while the 6th bag's MVP ($$1\,800\text{ Nakfa}$$) is below it, so the 6th bag would cost more than it returns.
why: **State the two formulas needed.** Marginal Product is $$\text{MP} = \frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}$$ and Marginal Value Product is $$\text{MVP} = \text{MP} \times P_y$$, where $$P_y$$ is the unit price of the output. Profit is maximized where $$\text{MVP} = P_x$$.

**Compute the marginal products.** Fourth bag: $$28 - 22 = 6\text{ quintals}$$. Fifth bag: $$32 - 28 = 4\text{ quintals}$$. Sixth bag: $$34 - 32 = 2\text{ quintals}$$. MP is falling, which is the Law of Diminishing Marginal Returns in action.

**Compute the marginal value products.** $$\text{MVP} = \text{MP} \times 900\text{ Nakfa}$$. Fourth bag: $$6 \times 900 = 5\,400\text{ Nakfa}$$. Fifth bag: $$4 \times 900 = 3\,600\text{ Nakfa}$$. Sixth bag: $$2 \times 900 = 1\,800\text{ Nakfa}$$.

**Compare each MVP with the input price.** The price of the input is $$P_x = 2\,000\text{ Nakfa}$$ per bag. The fourth bag adds $$5\,400\text{ Nakfa}$$ of value for $$2\,000\text{ Nakfa}$$, the fifth adds $$3\,600\text{ Nakfa}$$, and the sixth adds only $$1\,800\text{ Nakfa}$$.

**Identify the profit-maximizing level.** The fifth bag still gives $$\text{MVP} = 3\,600\text{ Nakfa} > P_x = 2\,000\text{ Nakfa}$$, so it is worth applying. The sixth bag gives $$\text{MVP} = 1\,800\text{ Nakfa} < P_x = 2\,000\text{ Nakfa}$$, so it is not worth applying. The profit-maximizing level is therefore $$5$$ bags.

**Explain the loss from over-application.** At the sixth bag the farmer pays $$2\,000\text{ Nakfa}$$ and receives output worth only $$1\,800\text{ Nakfa}$$, a net loss of $$200\text{ Nakfa}$$. All the levels examined still lie in Stage II, where MP is positive but falling; pushing inputs until MP becomes negative would enter Stage III, the irrational zone of waste.

questions.q: Management (entrepreneurship) is described as the factor of production that combines land, labour and capital. Explain why management is regarded as the coordinating force among the other three factors of production, and contrast the main management objective of a commercial farm in Eritrea with that of a subsistence farm.
questions.answer: Management coordinates the other factors because it is the only human resource that combines land, labour and capital, makes the business decisions through planning, implementation and control, and bears all the risks of success or failure. A commercial farm aims at profit maximisation or cost minimisation, while a subsistence farm aims at household self-sufficiency rather than profit.
why: **Identify what each factor can and cannot do alone.** Land (soil, water and climate) has a fixed supply and is immobile; labour is the physical and mental contribution of humans; capital is the human-made asset set, either fixed or working. None of these three can decide by itself how much of the others to use.

**State the function of management.** Management is the human resource responsible for combining land, labour and capital, making the business decisions, and bearing all the risks of success or failure. It is therefore the decision-making and organisational factor.

**Explain the coordinating role.** The farm manager performs the functions of planning, implementation and control. Planning decides the enterprise and input levels, implementation organises land, labour and capital into actual production, and control compares results with the plan, so the three physical factors are only brought together and adjusted through management.

**State the commercial-farm objective.** On a commercial farm the main objective is the maximisation of profit or the minimisation of production costs, so decisions are driven by returns compared with costs.

**State the subsistence-farm objective and conclude.** On a subsistence farm the main objective is not profit but achieving household self-sufficiency, so the same resources are organised to feed the household first. In both cases, however, it is management that decides, bears the risk, and coordinates land, labour and capital.

**Classify Farm X.** Selling the whole harvest on the market is commercial farming, where the main objective is the maximisation of profit or the minimisation of production costs.
**Classify Farm Y.** Consuming most of the harvest at home means the main objective is not profit but achieving household self-sufficiency.

**Compare the risks borne.** Management is the factor that bears all risks of success or failure. Farm X's manager carries price and market risk on the whole output, whereas Farm Y's manager is largely shielded from price risk and mainly faces weather, pest and yield risk.
**Conclude.** Identical land and labour produce different decisions because the management objective differs: profit maximisation on Farm X and household self-sufficiency on Farm Y.
